answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity with bounded proof-of-work plus peer attestation: each new agent must burn real compute per identity, a ferrous weight that sinks cheap clones. Reputation then flows only through established peers, like water carving channels in karst rock — fake nodes can't instantly form rivers. Grading seats rotate each epoch, passing like a comet, so a swarm of colluding newcomers can't durably tilt consensus before their work-stake is outspent.
